terms.comment: With an accusative, an accusative and infinitive (realise that), or a question: Num tū intellegis hīc quid narret? (Ter. Ph. 846). Nōn satis intellegō: I don’t quite understand (Traupman 110). Lewis & Short calls intelligō “less correct”.

phrases.latin: Num tū intellegis hīc quid narret? — Num tū? — Nihil. — Tantundem ego.
phrases.english: Do you understand what he’s saying? — Do you? — Not a thing. — Nor do I.

phrases.latin: quārē nōn, ut intellegere possit, sed, nē omnīnō possit nōn intellegere, cūrandum
phrases.english: so we must take care not that he can understand, but that he cannot possibly fail to understand

phrases.latin: avāritia vērō senīlis quid sibi velit, nōn intellegō
phrases.english: but what an old man’s greed is for, I do not understand

phrases.latin: ō mē īnfēlīcem! quī nunc dēmum intellegō ūtilia mihi quam fuerint quae dēspexeram
phrases.english: poor me! only now do I realise how useful to me were the things I had despised
